match.reason: No point in the bank covers converting units of length, area, volume, mass or capacity, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Unit conversions
card: Length, mass and capacity: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 km = 1000 m, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 L = 1000 mL. To go to a smaller unit, multiply. To go to a larger unit, divide.
For area, square the length factor. 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm². For volume, cube it: 1 m³ = 100 × 100 × 100 = 1 000 000 cm³.
1 cm³ holds 1 mL. So 1000 cm³ holds 1000 mL, which is 1 L.
Worked example: 30 000 cm² to m². Divide by 10 000, because 1 m² = 10 000 cm². The answer is 3 m².
draft.remember: Square the length factor for area and cube it for volume. 1 cm³ = 1 mL.

a.q: A rug has an area of 50 000 cm². What is its area in m²?
a.why: 1 m² = 10 000 cm², so divide: 50 000 ÷ 10 000 = 5 m². Dividing by 1000 or 100 gives 50 or 500, which wrongly uses the length factor for an area.
a.clue: How many cm² are in 1 m²?

b.q: Priya's fish tank is a box 50 cm long, 20 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is full of water. How many litres does it hold?
b.why: Volume = 50 × 20 × 30 = 30 000 cm³. Since 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, that is 30 000 mL, and dividing by 1000 gives 30 L. Dividing by 100 instead gives 300 L, which mixes up the factor for mL to L.
b.clue: Find the volume in cm³ first, then change mL to L.

problems.detail: The why says dividing by 1000 or by 100 'wrongly uses the length factor'. Only 100 is the cm-to-m length factor. Dividing by 1000 is not the length factor for cm to m, so the explanation of the 50 m² distractor is inaccurate.

The question needs the volume of a rectangular prism (length × width × height), which belongs to point 6 (Volume and capacity) and is not taught on this card. The conversion itself is covered, but the volume step is not.

check.summary: Both answers are correct (5 m² and 30 L). Question b relies on finding a box's volume, which belongs to the later volume point, and the why for a wrongly calls dividing by 1000 a use of the length factor.
